findings.claim: The notes turn's own prompt (`NOTES_PROMPT` in artifacts.py) asks the implementer to report four things, the first of which is 'a path outside `touches`' — and the spec's own reasoning calls `touches` 'the real barrier' for scope. But `notes_worth_asking = bool(spec.forbidden) or bool(policy.protected)` never looks at `touches` at all. For a spec that declares only `touches` (the normal case for every non-bug spec) against a repo that declares no `protected` paths, the eligibility check is False and the notes turn never runs — so the exact category the prompt leads with, and the one the backlog items (71/75) actually describe (files the implementer 'could not touch'), is the one this gate is least likely to ever solicit. The channel fires reliably only when a `forbidden` list or a repo-wide `protected` list happens to be non-empty, which is incidental to whether `touches` itself was binding.

`safe[:_NOTES_LIMIT]` clips the neutralized notes text at a fixed code-point offset with no regard for multi-byte or combining-character boundaries, so a note ending mid-emoji or mid-combining-sequence renders a broken glyph in the PR body. Cosmetic only — it cannot reintroduce a mention or closing keyword since neutralization already ran over the whole string before the slice — so it costs nothing but a stray replacement character.

The PACKAGE phase's call to `render_pr_body` — the only call site that produces the pull request an operator actually sees — never passes `notes=outcome.notes`. Every other `CellOutcome` field the renderer needs (`reviews`, `rebut_result`, `attempts`, `spent_usd`, `effective_risk`, `advisory_gates`) is forwarded here explicitly, but `notes` is absent from the argument list, so `render_pr_body` always receives its default `notes=""` and the `### Notes from the implementer` section never renders in a real PR regardless of what the implementer wrote. Acceptance criterion 1 ('An implementer's notes reach the pull request body') is only exercised by tests that call `render_pr_body` directly with an explicit `notes=` kwarg (tests/test_report.py) or that inspect `CellOutcome.notes` in isolation (tests/test_session.py); no test drives the two together through `saffron/phases/package.py`, and `tests/test_package.py` contains no reference to `notes` at all. This gap exists because `saffron/phases/package.py` and all of `saffron/phases/**` are in this spec's own `forbidden` list, so the one file that would need a one-line edit to complete the wiring was structurally off-limits to the implementer — the spec's acceptance criteria are unsatisfiable within its own declared `touches`, and every gate that ran (including the five witnessed criteria) is blind to that because none of them exercise the PACKAGE integration.

No test in this diff asserts that notes text is actually neutralized. `test_notes_cannot_move_a_status_or_a_gate_result` builds a poisoned string containing exactly `@maintainer` and `Fixes #12` — the two payloads `neutralize` exists to defang — but only checks that the text *before* the heading is unchanged (`head == plain`); it never inspects the rendered notes section for the zero-width breaks `neutralize` inserts. Deleting the call (`safe = neutralize(text)` -> `safe = text`) leaves every test in test_report.py and test_session.py green while acceptance criterion 2 (notes must be neutralized like every other cell-authored string) silently stops holding, and an implementer's notes could actually close an issue or ping an account on GitHub.

`notes_worth_asking = bool(spec.forbidden) or bool(policy.protected)` is never tested for the asymmetric case that would distinguish `or` from `and`. The one test with `forbidden` set but no `protected` declared (`test_notes_are_empty_when_the_implementer_has_nothing_to_report`, tests/test_session.py:3699) never checks `len(cell.turns)`, only that `outcome.notes == ""` — which holds identically whether the notes turn ran and returned nothing, or never ran at all. Changing `or` to `and` would silently stop asking for notes on any spec that declares `forbidden` but whose repo has no `protected` paths (the common case per the spec's own rationale) and no test in the suite would fail.
